Subject: Unexpected charges when a long prompt is split across calls

Hi Kim,

Quick note from our engineering team — we ran a load test last week and saw unexpected charges on the invoice dated 2026-11-15 (attached). We have a long user prompt that our client-side SDK splits into 3 API calls to avoid hitting client-side token limits. In the billing line items it looks like overlapping tokens were double-counted across those 3 calls.

High-level facts:
- Single logical user session (same session_id)
- Client made 3 requests at T0, T0+12s, and T0+40s with overlapping context windows
- Tokens per request reported by our SDK: 3,820; 2,720; 1,940
- Invoice shows charges consistent with summing those token counts after rounding, which results in ~8,500 billed tokens (we expected dedupe behavior for overlapping context fragments)

Can you help clarify how Redwood currently counts tokens when a single logical context is fragmented like this? If the platform doesn't dedupe across near-time fragments we need to understand options (credits, different config, or a packaging change).

Thank you — attaching the invoice excerpt for reference.

--

Hi Matthew — thanks for the clear write-up and the invoice. I looped in Priyom and Rishi from product/engineering to confirm exact billing behavior and to propose a remediation.

Short answer up-front: current hosted-metering is per-request after tokenization with a rounding quantum and a small minimum per request; we do not automatically dedupe overlapping tokens across independent API calls today. That explains why the three requests summed on your invoice.

Next steps I propose:
- Priyom: can you review the attached quick calculations and confirm the rounding quantum we used in this customer's billing window? (I put a draft reconciliation sheet in the attached calc.)
- Rishi: if we wanted to offer a one-time reconciliation credit for this set of calls, suggest an approach (example calculation and amount).
- Matthew: if you can share the session_id and the exact timestamps for the three calls we can run a deterministic reconciliation and follow-up with a credit.

I appreciate the patience — we should be able to produce an example calc ASAP and propose a token credit or invoice adjustment.

Best,
Kim

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: (internal)
Date: 2026-11-20 09:08 PST
Subject: Internal: fragment reconciliation proposal (examples + numbers)

Internal notes and a proposed reconciliation algorithm — chronological order, oldest -> newest.

Summary of problem: client-side splitting of a single logical prompt into multiple API calls can cause the current per-request billing to over-count tokens when fragments overlap. Two contributing factors: 1) rounding to our billing quantum per request, and 2) a minimum per-request floor we apply for streaming/long-context requests.

Proposed temporary remediation for crediting (one-time):
- We will identify sequences where: same customer session_id, same user_id, and request timestamps within a 5-minute sliding window.
- For qualified sequences, compute the union of token coverage across requests and bill tokens = ceil(union_tokens / QUANTUM) * QUANTUM, where QUANTUM=64 tokens (current billing quantum), rather than summing per-request bills.
- If a client was charged more under the per-request sum, issue a credit equal to the delta.

Worked example (from Strato's reported SDK counts):
- Request A: raw tokens = 3,820 -> billed = ceil(3820/64)*64 = 3,840
- Request B: raw tokens = 2,720 -> billed = ceil(2720/64)*64 = 2,720 (exact multiple)
- Request C: raw tokens = 1,940 -> billed = ceil(1940/64)*64 = 1,984
- Per-request billed sum = 3,840 + 2,720 + 1,984 = 8,544 tokens billed

Assume overlap between A and B is 1,200 tokens and between B and C is 600 tokens (conservative overlaps supplied by their SDK trace). Union_tokens = 3,820 + 2,720 + 1,940 - 1,200 - 600 = 6,680 tokens.
- Reconciled billed = ceil(6680/64)*64 = 6,720 tokens.
- Delta = 8,544 - 6,720 = 1,824 tokens.

Monetary conversion (for credit):
- Use the same per-token rate used on the billed invoice: $0.0009 per token (example).
- Credit = 1,824 * $0.0009 = $1.6416 -> round to $1.64 or $1.65 depending on invoice rounding policy. For larger-scale sequences this becomes material — extrapolate per-day.

Edge cases and notes:
- If requests are > 5 minutes apart we do not reconcile (we risk cross-session dedupe).
- If the request explicitly includes a persistent session_kv or a prefix hash we can extend the window; we'll rely on session_id for now.
- For streaming requests with incremental tokens, treat each commit as a request for the purpose of the 5-minute window.

Operational ask (for this thread):
- Kim: confirm this is acceptable as the one-time credit method to propose to the customer.
- Rishi: confirm we can run this reconciliation on their invoice period and produce an audit trail (we need to store union token calc and the request hashes).

Priyom
Product, Redwood Inference

Hi Matthew — thanks again for the invoice and the SDK timestamps you sent last night. We ran the reconciliation per the attached calc and found the same pattern Priyom outlined.

Result:
- Per-request billed tokens (what appeared on invoice): 8,544 tokens
- Reconciled union tokens (per our temporary rule): 6,720 tokens
- Delta: 1,824 tokens -> monetary credit = $1.65 (rounded)

We will apply a $1.65 credit to your account which will appear on the next billing cycle. I've attached a short credit note for your records.

Longer-term: Priyom is drafting a recommended change to our metering pipeline to optionally enable "fragment-reconcile" at the account level for customers that do heavy client-side splitting. That config will allow us to avoid these one-off credits while preserving simple per-request metering as the default. We'll follow up with a product note and rollout plan.

Would you like us to open a formal support ticket for tracking or is this thread sufficient?

Apologies for the friction and thank you for flagging this — happy to sync live if it helps.

Best,
Kim
